queries.query: Our PR build takes 35 minutes. Where is the time going and how do we speed up the GitHub Actions workflow?
Make dotnet-build.yml faster; the build and the specs run one after the other in a single job.
Jobs sit in the queue for ten minutes before they start. Is it the number of jobs or the runners?
Add NuGet and Yarn caching to our workflows so CI stops restoring everything on every run.
Docs-only pull requests still run the whole pipeline. Add path filters without making required checks hang.
We burn too many runner minutes on pull requests that get superseded and cancelled. Reduce the waste.
Our publish workflow rebuilds everything that the PR run already built and tested. Make it publish the tested artifacts.
Merged releases are being dropped when two PRs merge close together; the publish workflow cancels or loses the pending run.
Prove the CI change helped: compare workflow wall clock and runner-minutes before and after.
Docker image builds in CI take eight minutes every time even when nothing changed. Add a buildx layer cache.
Draft the release notes for version 3.4 from the merged pull requests.
Which assurance tier does this release need, and do we need an SBOM and provenance?
CI is red on my pull request. Fix the failing test.
The same checkout screen keeps breaking every sprint. Why do we keep fixing the same bug?
Our command handler is slow under load and the read model query times out in production.
queries.note: application runtime performance: cratis-performance-review should win

queries.query: Run the local build and specs before I push so I know the change is safe.
queries.note: local gates before pushing; not CI workflow speed

queries.query: Review this workflow for script injection and over-broad token permissions.
queries.note: security review: cratis-security-review should win; no speed question

queries.query: Write a documentation page explaining how our release pipeline works for new contributors.
